Symptoms: White/gray fuzzy patches on mouth, gills, or body. Ulcers. Rapid breathing.
Causes: Poor water quality, high temperature, stress, overcrowding.
Treatment Plan: 1. Isolate fish. 2. Lower temp slightly. 3. Treat with Kanamycin (Kanaplex) + Nitrofurazone (Furan-2) combination. 4. Improve aeration and water changes.
Betta / Extra Notes: Often mistaken for fungus in Bettas. Highly lethal; requires immediate antibiotic treatment.

Symptoms: Edges of fins turning white, black, or red. Fins fraying or melting away.
Causes: Ammonia/Nitrite spikes, poor hygiene, nipping from tank mates.
Treatment Plan: 1. Check water parameters (Ammonia must be 0). 2. 50% water change. 3. Treat with Erythromycin or Maracyn. 4. Add aquarium salt (1 tbsp per 3 gallons) if freshwater.
Betta / Extra Notes: Extremely common in Bettas kept in unfiltered bowls. Clean water is the primary cure.

Symptoms: Severe bloating, scales protruding outward like a pinecone, lethargy.
Causes: Advanced internal bacterial infection, prolonged stress, poor diet.
Treatment Plan: 1. Immediate isolation. 2. Epsom salt baths (1 tbsp per gallon for 15 mins) to draw out fluids. 3. Strong antibiotics in food (Kanaplex + Focus). 4. Prognosis is generally poor.
Betta / Extra Notes: Bettas are highly susceptible. Often fatal by the time pineconing appears.

Symptoms: Small white spots resembling salt grains on body and fins. Flashing (scratching against objects).
Causes: Introduction of new infected fish/plants, temperature drops suppressing immune system.
Treatment Plan: 1. Raise temperature to 86°F (30°C) gradually. 2. Add Aquarium Salt. 3. Treat with Copper-based meds or Formalin/Malachite Green (e.g., Seachem ParaGuard or Ich-X). 4. Treat entire tank.
Betta / Extra Notes: Bettas tolerate heat well; raising temp above 84F accelerates parasite life cycle to be killed by meds.

Symptoms: Dusty, yellowish-gold film on body. Clamped fins, heavy breathing, scratching.
Causes: Stress, poor water conditions, newly introduced fish. Parasite uses photosynthesis.
Treatment Plan: 1. Turn off all aquarium lights (blackout). 2. Raise temperature slightly. 3. Treat with Copper sulfate or Malachite Green. 4. Add Aquarium salt.
Betta / Extra Notes: Very common in Bettas. Use a flashlight in a dark room to see the gold dust on the Betta's body.

Symptoms: Gasping at surface, red/swollen gills, excessive slime coat, scratching.
Causes: Overcrowding, poor water quality, transmitted from unquarantined fish.
Treatment Plan: 1. Treat with Praziquantel (PraziPro). 2. Treat the entire display tank. 3. Do a second treatment 5-7 days later to kill hatching eggs.
Betta / Extra Notes: Can quickly suffocate Bettas. Praziquantel is highly effective and safe for them.

Symptoms: Actual fluffy cotton-like growths on body, usually growing out of a wound or dead tissue.
Causes: Secondary infection on an open wound, ulcer, or due to extreme temperature drops.
Treatment Plan: 1. Isolate fish. 2. Treat with Methylene Blue baths or Malachite Green. 3. Maintain pristine water quality to let wound heal.
Betta / Extra Notes: Bettas attacking each other often get fungal infections on the bite wounds.

Symptoms: Red/purple gills, gasping for air at surface, lethargy, red streaks on fins/body.
Causes: Uncycled tank, broken nitrogen cycle, overfeeding, dead fish decomposing.
Treatment Plan: 1. IMMEDIATE 50-75% water change. 2. Dose Seachem Prime to detoxify remaining ammonia. 3. Stop feeding for 3 days. 4. Add beneficial bacteria.
Betta / Extra Notes: The #1 killer of Bettas in uncycled bowls. Not a disease, but an environmental crisis.

Symptoms: Gasping at surface, rapid gill movement, brown gills.
Treatment Plan: 1. 50% water change. 2. Add aquarium salt (chloride protects gills from nitrite). 3. Dose Seachem Prime.
Betta / Extra Notes: Salt is the specific antidote for nitrite toxicity in freshwater fish.

Symptoms: Pitting or small holes forming on the head and lateral line. White stringy feces.
Causes: Poor diet, poor water quality, carbon dust, flagellate parasite.
Treatment Plan: 1. Improve diet (high-quality varied foods). 2. Treat with Metronidazole (Metroplex) in food. 3. Large water changes.
Betta / Extra Notes: More common in Cichlids, but can affect Bettas if diet is extremely poor.
